description_eng: Jewish Kingdom of Himyar (Yemen, Najran and Hadramawt core)
description_heb: ממלכת חִמיָר היהודית (ליבת תימן, נג'ראן וחדרמות)
verbatim_quote: Judaism became the de facto state religion after the reign of Malkikarib Yuhamin (c. 375-400 CE)
outline_basis: Schematic outline of the core named in the article (southern highlands of Yemen, Najran, Hadramawt conquered c. 300). Not the kingdom's maximal extent in central Arabia. No border treaty exists; vertices are approximate.

description_eng: Khazar Khaganate (Jewish ruling elite from the 8th century)
description_heb: הכאגנות החזרית (העילית השלטת התגיירה במאה ה-8)
verbatim_quote: dominated the vast area extending from the Volga-Don steppes to the eastern Crimea and the northern Caucasus
outline_basis: Outline traced from the article phrase (Volga-Don steppes, eastern Crimea, northern Caucasus, Caspian shore) and a general atlas picture; boundaries of nomadic realms were fluid and the article gives 650-969 in the infobox but 650-965 in body text.

description_eng: Pale of Settlement (Jewish residence restricted to the western Russian Empire)
description_heb: תחום המושב (הגבלת מגורי היהודים במערב האימפריה הרוסית)
verbatim_quote: The Pale came into being under the rule of Catherine the Great in 1791.
outline_basis: Approximate union of the governorates the article lists (Mogilev, Kiev, Chernigov, Poltava, Ekaterinoslav, Taurida, Minsk, Volhynia, Podolia, Vilna, Grodno); Bessarabia, Kherson and Congress Poland (added later) included from general knowledge, not the fetched page; Kiev city exclusion not drawn; Vitebsk partly omitted. Simplified to 25 vertices.

description_eng: Crown of Aragon on the Iberian mainland (Aragon, Catalonia, Valencia) with its Jewish aljamas until 1492
description_heb: כתר אראגון בחצי האי האיברי (אראגון, קטלוניה, ולנסיה) וקהילות היהודים בו עד 1492
verbatim_quote: The Crown of Aragon and its institutions and public law were abolished between 1707 and 1716.
outline_basis: Mainland envelope of Aragon, Catalonia and Valencia from the territory list in the Crown of Aragon article (Aragon + Barcelona 1162, Valencia 1238); Balearics, Sicily, Sardinia and Naples not drawn; Roussillon omitted. Jewish expulsion of 1492 from the History of the Jews in Spain article. Coastline traced from general atlas knowledge.

description_eng: Crown of Castile (Castile, Leon, Galicia, Andalusia, Murcia) with its Jewish aljamas until 1492
description_heb: כתר קסטיליה וקהילות היהודים בו עד 1492
verbatim_quote: The article says the Crown formed in 1230 and lists Murcia (1258) and Granada (1492).
outline_basis: Rough envelope of the Castilian realm east of the Portuguese border, from the territory list (Castile, Leon, Galicia, Cordoba/Jaen/Seville 1236-1248, Murcia 1258; Granada 1492 included on the south coast). Border vertices from general atlas knowledge. Expulsion data from History of the Jews in Spain article.

description_eng: Council of Four Lands (Greater Poland, Lesser Poland, Galicia, Volhynia) - Jewish autonomy
description_heb: מועצת ארבע הארצות - אוטונומיה יהודית (פולין הגדולה, פולין הקטנה, גליציה, וולהיניה)
verbatim_quote: from the second half of the 16th century to 1764
outline_basis: Envelope of the four lands named in the article within the Crown of Poland (Greater Poland, Lesser Poland, Galicia with Podolia, Volhynia); the separate Lithuanian council is not covered. Outline from a general map of the pre-partition Polish Crown, approximate.

verbatim_quote: It included the historical regions of Judea, Samaria and the coastal plain.
outline_basis: Combined envelope of the three provinces from the article (Prima: Judea, Samaria, coast, capital Caesarea; Secunda: northern Transjordan, Jezreel, Galilee, Golan; Salutaris: Negev, southern Transjordan, part of Sinai). Eastern desert limits are guesses.

description_eng: Sasanian Babylonia (Asoristan) - home of the Babylonian Talmudic academies
verbatim_quote: Asoristan was largely identical with ancient Mesopotamia.
outline_basis: Northern limit per the article (line from Anatha to Takrit), southernmost point Hira; west edge at the desert and east edge at the Zagros foothills are approximate.

description_eng: Ottoman Mutasarrifate of Jerusalem (Jerusalem, Hebron, Jaffa, Gaza, Beersheba)
description_heb: המוטסריפות של ירושלים העות'מאנית (ירושלים, חברון, יפו, עזה ובאר שבע)
verbatim_quote: under the direct authority of the Ottoman government in Constantinople
outline_basis: Article: encompassed Jerusalem, Hebron, Jaffa, Gaza and Beersheba, from the Mediterranean to the Jordan River and Dead Sea (c. 12,486 km2 in 1862). The northern limit and the Negev extent are approximate. Beersheba sanjak (1900) postdates 1872.

description_eng: British Mandate Palestine (west of the Jordan River)
outline_basis: Outline follows the commonly mapped 1923 boundary (Lebanon border at Rosh Hanikra and Metula, the Syrian line east of the Hula and Sea of Galilee, Yarmuk and Jordan, Wadi Araba to Aqaba, Taba-Rafah Egypt line). The cited page gave only dates and area (25,585 km2); coordinates are from general geographic knowledge. Transjordan (east of the Jordan) is excluded.

description_eng: UN Partition Plan 1947 - proposed Jewish state, Eastern Galilee section (schematic)
description_heb: תוכנית החלוקה 1947 - המדינה היהודית המוצעת, חלק הגליל המזרחי (סכמטי)
verbatim_quote: the fertile Eastern Galilee, the Coastal Plain, stretching from Haifa to Rehovot
outline_basis: Resolution 181 gave the Jewish state three sections (Eastern Galilee; the coast from Haifa to Rehovot; most of the Negev). The fetched article names the regions but not the exact boundary lines, so these three polygons are intentionally rough envelopes, not the UN map. Replace with a digitised map before use.

description_eng: UN Partition Plan 1947 - proposed Jewish state, Coastal Plain section (schematic)
description_heb: תוכנית החלוקה 1947 - המדינה היהודית המוצעת, מישור החוף (סכמטי)
verbatim_quote: the Coastal Plain, stretching from Haifa to Rehovot
outline_basis: Rough envelope of the coastal strip from Haifa to Rehovot (the Jaffa enclave not cut out). Same caveat as the Eastern Galilee polygon.

description_eng: UN Partition Plan 1947 - proposed Jewish state, Negev section (schematic)
description_heb: תוכנית החלוקה 1947 - המדינה היהודית המוצעת, הנגב (סכמטי)
verbatim_quote: most of the Negev desert, including the southern outpost of Umm Rashrash
outline_basis: Rough envelope; Beersheba and the strip along the Egyptian border were assigned to the Arab state in the final plan, which this outline only crudely respects.

description_eng: Israel within the 1949 armistice lines (Green Line)
verbatim_quote: demarcation line set out in the 1949 Armistice Agreements
outline_basis: Article describes the Green Line only as the 1949 armistice demarcation and does not give its course. Outline from general map knowledge (West Bank west edge, Gaza Strip carved out, Negev to Eilat); the divided Jerusalem line is simplified. Do not use for border claims.

description_eng: Jewish Autonomous Oblast (Birobidzhan), Soviet Far East
description_heb: המחוז האוטונומי היהודי (בירובידג'אן), המזרח הרחוק הסובייטי
outline_basis: Article gives centre 48 deg 36 N 132 deg 12 E, area 36,271 km2, neighbours Khabarovsk Krai, Amur Oblast and Heilongjiang (China); it gives no outline. Polygon is a schematic envelope centred there and sized to roughly that area; Amur river border on the south not traced. Year_end 1991 is the end of the USSR (oblast continues in Russia).
